product: Secure Firewall ASA Software and Cisco Secure FTD Software
campaign_note: Cisco PSIRT reported active exploitation of an unauthenticated SSL remote-access VPN reload (DoS) bug in October 2026; Cisco disclosed no attacker, victim, or scale details and no outage reports were found.

first_exploitation_claim.source: Cisco PSIRT advisory cisco-sa-asaftd-tunnel-dos-s6mgkb75 ("In October 2026, the Cisco PSIRT became aware of active exploitation of this vulnerability.")

evidence.counts_what: Cisco ASA SSL VPN devices exposed online (exposure of the product/service, not confirmed-vulnerable configurations and not crashed devices)
evidence.measured_on: 2026-10-29 (article date; article says 'currently', no explicit measurement date)
evidence.quote: Internet monitoring platform Shadowserver tracks more than 51,000 Cisco ASA SSL VPN devices exposed online.

campaign_note: Nextcloud administrators reported PHP webshells planted via richdocumentscode proxy.php from 2026-09-10, about a month before the advisory and CVE; the only counts are a handful of administrator self-reports and the total number of servers hit is explicitly unknown.

first_exploitation_claim.source: The Hacker News, citing administrator reports on GitHub and Collabora's 14 October advisory; first logged attack dated 2026-09-10

evidence.counts_what: Nextcloud administrators who reported attacks on their instances on GitHub (self-reports; a floor, not a campaign total)
evidence.measured_by: Administrator reports on GitHub, as summarized by The Hacker News
evidence.quote: Three administrators reported the issue on GitHub, with the first logged attack on September 10.

evidence.counts_what: Additional administrators reporting the same activity on their own instances (self-reports)
evidence.measured_by: Administrator reports, as summarized by The Hacker News
evidence.quote: Two other administrators reported the same on their own instances.

evidence.counts_what: Explicit statement that no total count of affected servers exists
evidence.quote: How many servers were hit is not known.

evidence.counts_what: Post-exploitation activity on affected servers; ransomware use is user-reported and not confirmed by the outlet
evidence.quote: Some users also reported that ransomware operators are exploiting the flaw.

campaign_note: The vendor's 2026-10-14 alert and JPCERT/CC alert JPCERT-AT-2026-0032 state exploitation is confirmed, but no source gives attacker, victim, install-base, or scale information.

first_exploitation_claim.source: EG Secure Solutions alert (vendor); page states support-contract customers were notified separately on 2026-09-29

campaign_note: Fortinet advisory FG-IR-26-122 (published 2026-04-14) carries a 'Known Exploited: Yes' flag with no description of the exploitation; no press or telemetry reporting on in-the-wild use was found.

first_exploitation_claim.date: unknown (advisory published 2026-04-14; the date the 'Known Exploited: Yes' flag was set is not shown; CISA KEV addition 2026-10-16)
first_exploitation_claim.source: Fortinet PSIRT advisory FG-IR-26-122, 'Known Exploited' field

campaign_note: The project's GitHub advisory reports in-the-wild exploitation against a single v2.1.1 deployment (custom backends running reverse shells), reported by Javier Sixto (ulex.fr); no exposure or wider compromise counts were found from reputable sources.

evidence.counts_what: A single GPUStack v2.1.1 deployment observed exploited; the advisory gives no numeric count
evidence.measured_by: GPUStack maintainers, on a report from Javier Sixto (ulex.fr)
evidence.quote: has been observed exploited in the wild against a v2.1.1 deployment.

campaign_note: Patched 2026-10-12 with a Rapid7 PoC on 2026-10-13; Alpine Linux disclosed exploitation attempts against its GitLab instance on 20-21 October (success not confirmed, instance rebuilt), and CISA added the CVE to KEV on 2026-10-29.

first_exploitation_claim.source: Alpine Linux incident post (attempts on 2026-10-20 and 2026-10-21); CISA KEV listing followed on 2026-10-29

evidence.counts_what: Internet-facing hosts running a GitLab version affected by this CVE (also 79,224 web properties); version-based, out of 82,454 GitLab hosts detected
evidence.measured_on: 2026-10-13 (advisory date; no separate measurement date stated)
evidence.quote: Censys currently detects 25,766 hosts and 79,224 web properties with a version of GitLab affected by this vulnerability.

evidence.counts_what: All internet-facing hosts running GitLab (denominator for the vulnerable count; also 205,541 web properties)
evidence.quote: We currently detect 82,454 hosts and 205,541 web properties running GitLab, based on the following query

evidence.counts_what: GitLab instances still vulnerable to CVE-2026-97229 about three weeks after the patch
evidence.quote: We are currently tracking over 1000 GitLab instances vulnerable to CVE-2026-97229 (on @CISACyber KEV)

evidence.counts_what: Internet-exposed GitLab Community Edition instances (patch status not stated; inconsistent in scope with the ~39K daily instances Shadowserver cites elsewhere)
evidence.quote: Internet threat watchdog Shadowserver tracks nearly 2,800 Internet-exposed GitLab Community Edition instances

evidence.value: 1 named: Alpine Linux (attempted; success not confirmed)
evidence.counts_what: Named organization targeted with the exploit; the victim found no evidence of success but could not rule it out
evidence.quote: We have found no evidence that it succeeded, but we cannot rule it out.

evidence.counts_what: GitLab worker process crashes caused by the exploit attempts on Alpine Linux's instance
evidence.quote: This crashed GitLab worker processes 8 times.

evidence.value: instance closed to non-developers from 2026-10-27, rebuild complete 2026-10-28, reopened 2026-10-29 (no duration stated by the source)

evidence.quote: GitLab closed to everyone except developers and build servers; rebuild started
